title: LCR series circuit and power factor
topicTitle: LCR series circuit and power factor
notes: The average power in a series LCR circuit is V_rms I_rms cosφ, not the product of the rms voltage and current alone. The extra factor cosφ is the power factor.
From the impedance triangle, cosφ = R/Z. A circuit that is almost a pure resistor has Z near R and a power factor near 1. A circuit dominated by reactance has a small power factor.

At resonance X_L = X_C, φ = 0 and the power factor is 1. All of the average power is then the heating I_rms^2 R in the resistor. The inductor and capacitor still exchange energy, but their average contribution is zero.
A power factor of zero means the current is 90° out of phase with the voltage, as in a pure inductor or a pure capacitor. Energy sloshes back to the source.
A lagging power factor is the inductive case, common with motors. Capacitors are added in industry to pull the power factor back toward 1 so that the current, for a given useful power, is smaller.
The instantaneous power oscillates. The average is what the meter records. Quoting V I without cosφ overstates the power whenever the phase is not zero.
